items.title: Add support for `uvx python@latest`
items.reason: Tracks the same explicit latest-stable Python selector. It references the shared Python request parser, and its discussion covers whether latest means the newest downloadable or installed interpreter.

items.title: Support python@latest for newest, stable, discoverable Python
items.reason: Pre-existing implementation for astral-sh/uv#13535 that adds latest handling to shared Python request, discovery, and download code. Review is still resolving selection semantics and command coverage.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests for `3.x`, the exact invalid-download-request error, `python install 3`, `sync --python 3`, `.python-version`, setup-python, latest/newest stable Python, version ranges, interpreter resolution, installed-versus-download preference, and Python upgrade fixes. astral-sh/uv#18284 was ruled out because it updates a concrete pin; astral-sh/uv#7892 and merged astral-sh/uv#13954 only upgrade managed patch releases; astral-sh/uv#16333 concerns general lowest/highest resolution rather than an explicit latest selector.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#13535 already tracks the same underlying latest-stable Python request, and astral-sh/uv#13873 is a pre-existing open implementation in the shared Python request layer. The new report adds broader consumers, but that scope can be centralized in the existing discussion.
summary: astral-sh/uv#13535 is the canonical latest-Python request, with implementation underway in astral-sh/uv#13873. No separate prior request specifically for `3.x` across install, sync, and version files was found.
draft_response:
Thanks — the underlying latest-Python request is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#13535, with an open implementation in astral-sh/uv#13873. Although the existing example is `uvx python@latest`, the implementation is in the shared Python request and discovery layer. The review is still settling whether `latest` selects the newest stable download or the newest stable local interpreter.

The `uv python install`, `uv sync --python`, and `.python-version` coverage you describe is useful additional scope. Please add those use cases to astral-sh/uv#13535 so the syntax and behavior can be resolved in one place.
